players.product: all-flash arrays / DirectFlash modules (hyperscaler design win)

quarterly_data.signal: The second hyperscaler (announced August 10) is a top five hyperscaler: Everpure achieved a design win and signed a supply agreement for its hyperscale DirectFlash products. Only a de minimis revenue contribution is expected in fiscal year 2027, with a meaningful ramp beginning in fiscal year 2028. The deal took longer than anticipated because the hyperscaler would not award the design win until it had its own NAND supply contract in place; hyperscalers procure the NAND through their own supply chain, not Everpure. The integration and business model are substantially similar to the first customer, starting in warmer, higher-performance tiers. Going forward Everpure will discuss hyperscale as a product category rather than individual customers or design-win timing.
quarterly_data.figure: second top five hyperscaler design win + supply agreement; de minimis FY2027 revenue, meaningful ramp from FY2028

quarterly_data.signal: CEO expects large hyperscaler order commitments for DirectFlash to extend into calendar 2028, powering tens of exabytes of capacity — a multiple of this year's expectations; committed order volumes for FY2027 and FY2028 continue to grow. Hyperscale revenue was minimal in Q2, with the majority expected in H2 FY2027 at 75%-85% margins; the hyperscale contribution in guidance was 'mostly baked in' and on track. In hyperscale, DirectFlash is mainly replacing SSDs for now (HDD replacement once pricing comes back into line); the CTO cited 5 times more reliability on a component basis versus SSDs and 2, 3, 5 times the density.
quarterly_data.figure: hyperscaler order commitments into calendar 2028, tens of exabytes; hyperscale margins 75%-85%

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 growth was driven by price, mix and capacity per system offsetting lower system unit volumes: customers are buying fewer solutions at higher prices with terabyte capacity up, and Everpure is operating at a pricing level not seen in 10 years with demand resilient among top-tier enterprises. Deals above $5 million grew 59% and deals above $20 million grew 385%. Operating profit was $230 million (19.4% margin), up 77%; adjusted for the Evergreen//One acceleration, the CEO said growth is well above 40% year-over-year. International revenue was $498 million, up 75%, a record 42% of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: deals above $5 million +59%, above $20 million +385%; operating profit $230 million, 19.4% margin; international revenue $498 million, +75%

quarterly_data.signal: Supply: cash flow from operations was negative $136 million, mainly from strategic component purchases — primarily NAND and other key components, for the core business, not the hyperscale business — made to secure supply and mitigate further price increases; the CFO said the company now has sufficient supply coverage for the foreseeable future and that pricing has roughly caught up with component costs. Q2 pricing actions largely offset component cost increases; product gross margin was 66.2%, up 70 basis points sequentially. Capex was $101 million (approximately 9% of revenue), supporting hyperscale scaling and Evergreen//One and reflecting higher component prices. The CEO said concern about sourcing components to deliver has gone away.
quarterly_data.figure: operating cash flow negative $136 million on strategic NAND/component buys; capex $101 million (approximately 9% of revenue); product gross margin 66.2%

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance rationale: management raised H2 guidance because two concerns went away — component sourcing and customer response to far higher prices (Q2 was the first full quarter at the higher prices) — and it now has two quarters of visibility. Significant hyperscale product revenue is still expected in Q3 and Q4 based on order commitments through the hyperscale supply chain for DFM solutions. The company intends to keep operating at the low end of its 65%-70% product gross margin range and expects fiscal year 2027 free cash flow of $600 million to $800 million.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027 free cash flow $600 million to $800 million; product gross margin at low end of 65%-70%

quarterly_data.signal: Evergreen//One TCV has accelerated to an annualized run rate above $1 billion for fiscal year 2027, as Evergreen//One price increases were contained well below those on traditional product purchases; storage-as-a-service TCV increased 121% year-over-year to $277 million in Q2. Average contract length is between three and four years.
quarterly_data.figure: storage-as-a-service TCV $277 million, +121% YoY; Evergreen//One TCV run rate above $1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: AI storage wins: Samsung Electronics chose FlashBlade//S to support its advanced AI and research initiatives; a major global bank selected FlashBlade//S for its internal GPU-as-a-Service environment; STN, a large AI managed service provider, expanded its FlashBlade//EXA investment and an international HPC/AI computing provider selected FlashBlade//EXA for AI training. Everpure DataStream, built on NVIDIA's AI Data Platform, reached general availability with first sales this quarter, and the company sees a steady increase in GPU attachments for FlashBlade products.
